deckTitle: MedKayfab Dermatology 01: The Great Barrier Brawl

cards.power: The Cornified Envelope. Transforms from a living basement worker to dead waterproof stone.
cards.lore: Whipped to the top in only 4 days during Psoriasis, resulting in unfinished scale-ruins.
cards.gradeReason: Instant embodiment — Kevin IS the cornified layer, role crystal clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: flat wrestling card. Subject: brick-shaped cell with hardhat, climbing a wall. Mood: industrious stoic.

cards.power: The Tight Grip. Holds Kevins together so the wall doesn't disintegrate at a touch.
cards.lore: Kidnapped by Pemphigus assassins, causing a positive Nikolsky sign (the wall crumbles).
cards.gradeReason: Kidnapped by assassins — immediate theater, no explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: muscular glue-molecule character gripping two bricks together. Mood: tense defender.

cards.power: The UV Parasol. Produces pigment shields to protect DNA headquarters.
cards.lore: Evicted by the immune system during Vitiligo.
cards.gradeReason: UV Parasol is instantly visual; eviction drama lands hard.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: melanocyte figure holding giant melanin umbrella. Mood: protective, vibrant.

cards.power: Antigen Scouting. Intercepts intruders and sprints to the lymph node to call backup.
cards.lore: Responsible for the delayed reaction in Type IV contact allergies.
cards.gradeReason: Strong role, but 'call backup' is slightly abstract for instant performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: scout character with binoculars and Birbeck-granule badge, sprinting. Mood: urgent.

cards.power: The Auspitz Move. Scrape off Pete's armor, and he bleeds from capillary leaks.
cards.lore: T-cell driven turbo-reconstruction. Loves the Koebner phenomenon.
cards.gradeReason: Scrape off the armor — bleeds from below. Kapow. Instant clinical image.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: silver-plated wrestler with flaking armor revealing blood drops. Mood: aggressive, flaky.

cards.power: The Scratch Cycle. A leaky wall lets allergens seep in, triggering the itch-alarm.
cards.lore: Part of the Atopic Triad. Loves flexures and hates soap.
cards.gradeReason: Leaky Wall + Scratch Cycle = you know exactly what Alice makes you do.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: cracked-wall character scratching frantically, allergens pouring through gaps. Mood: itchy, relentless.

cards.power: The Flaccid Burst. Creates thin blisters that pop instantly, leaving raw flesh.
cards.lore: Anti-Desmoglein 3 antibodies destroy the bond just above the foundation.
cards.gradeReason: The Flaccid Burst says everything — visceral and immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: villain character popping soap-bubble blisters above a crumbling wall. Mood: fragile chaos.

cards.power: The Water Balloon. Creates firm, tense blisters that do not pop easily.
cards.lore: Targets Hemidesmosomes—the anchors holding the wall to the floor.
cards.gradeReason: Water Balloon is the perfect metaphor — you feel the tense pressure immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: stocky wrestler holding taut water balloons for skin. Mood: pressurized, threatening.

cards.power: The Golden Glue. Creates honey-colored crusts around the mouth.
cards.lore: Highly infectious. Exfoliatin toxins peel the top layer of skin.
cards.gradeReason: The name IS the power — Honey-Crust, Golden Glue. No translation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: sticky golden-crusted villain grinning around a dripping honeycomb mouth. Mood: contagious mischief.

cards.power: The Red Rising. A flaming red, sharply defined invasion with fever-fanfares.
cards.lore: Travels through lymphatic pathways, mostly Group A Strep.
cards.gradeReason: Fever-fanfares is vivid; sharp border is memorable — but needs table context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: red-armored warrior with sharp geometric boundary-lines, trumpet fanfare. Mood: dramatic proclamation.

cards.power: The Expanding Circle. Eats keratin.
cards.lore: Loves damp environments and is transmitted by pet sidekicks.
cards.gradeReason: Expanding Circle is solid geometry; LORE adds just enough without full punch.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: circular fungus character eating a keratin plank in expanding rings. Mood: patient, creeping.

cards.power: The Tunnel Trap. Digs finger-webs and wrist-burrows in the dark.
cards.lore: Type IV reaction to his waste. The whole family reacts.
cards.gradeReason: Midnight Itcher + Tunnel Trap = you're already scratching before reading twice.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: tiny mite with miner's helmet digging through skin at midnight. Mood: nocturnal, relentless.

cards.power: The Latent Sting. Sleeps in the ganglion, waking during stress to form vesicles.
cards.lore: Dew drops on a rose petal. Hal is a specialist in returning.
cards.gradeReason: Dew drops on a rose petal + specialist in returning = unforgettable elegance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: virus curled asleep in a nerve ganglion, awakening with dewdrop vesicles. Mood: dreamy menace.

cards.power: The Nerve Fire. Strict dermatomal distribution, burns along one side only.
cards.lore: After chickenpox, Zane hides. In weakness he burns his way out.
cards.gradeReason: Nerve Fire is great; lore has strong concept but runs slightly incomplete.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: fire-trail wrestler burning along a dermatomal stripe on one side. Mood: reawakening fury.

cards.power: The Dented Pearl. Small, flesh-colored papules with a central pit.
cards.lore: Common in kids. Contains highly infectious molluscum bodies.
cards.gradeReason: Dented Pearl is charming; LORE describes rather than invites performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: round pearly character with a belly button dimple, winking. Mood: cute but contagious.

cards.power: The Rough Patch. Builds cauliflower growths with tiny black dot capillaries.
cards.lore: Hijacks keratinocyte division to fuel her fortress construction.
cards.gradeReason: Fortress construction is perfect villain framing — Vivian has a project.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: spiky cauliflower-textured villain building a warty castle brick by brick. Mood: determined architect.

cards.power: The Slow Burrow. Grows slowly with a pearly sheen but burrows deeply through tissue.
cards.lore: Rarely metastasizes — proud of local destruction instead.
cards.gradeReason: Pearly One is evocative; POWER needed context to fully land at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: pearl-shelled wrestler tunneling downward slowly, wearing a smug smile. Mood: patient destruction.

cards.power: The Scaly Shield. Forms crusty, hyperkeratotic tumors that invade deep.
cards.lore: Appears on sun terraces (scalp, ears). High metastasis risk.
cards.gradeReason: Scabby One + Scaly Shield is good; lore is explanatory rather than performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: scaly armored wrestler with keratin-pearl crown on sun-burned head. Mood: rough, aggressive.

cards.power: The Stealth Attack. Disguises as a mole but sneaks into lymphatics. His depth decides the match.
cards.lore: ABCDE criteria. Measure the Breslow!
cards.gradeReason: His depth decides the match — Breslow as wrestling mechanic is pure brilliance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: shadowy mole-disguised villain infiltrating lymph vessels. Mood: sinister mimicry.

cards.power: The Rough Preview. Scaly, rough patch on sun-damaged skin.
cards.lore: Turns into Squamous-Sam if ignored.
cards.gradeReason: Sandpaper is tactile and immediate; lore threat is excellent but POWER underplays.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: rough-textured character on sun-baked ground, crouching before evolving. Mood: prequel energy.

cards.power: The Purple Patch. Forms pruritic purple polygonal papules with white lace lines.
cards.lore: T-cell attack on the dermo-epidermal junction. Loves wrists and mucous membranes.
cards.gradeReason: Purple Polygon as STAT is genius; alliterative POWER lands instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: purple geometric wrestler with white lace tattoos on wrists. Mood: elegant menace.

cards.power: The Central Flush. Persistent redness and visible vessels across nose and cheeks.
cards.lore: Triggered by spices, alcohol, heat. Can lead to rhinophyma in men.
cards.gradeReason: Flush Queen is immediately performable — you can blush on command.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: rosy-cheeked queen with red-veined nose, flushing on a throne. Mood: regal and inflamed.

cards.power: The Shin Bruiser. Tender, red nodules erupt on the shins.
cards.lore: Reaction to infections, sarcoidosis, or meds. Pain before clarity.
cards.gradeReason: Shin Bruiser is tactile; LORE explains triggers without inviting performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: painful red-nodule character sitting on shins with mystery-sign expression. Mood: reactive, bruised.

cards.power: The 24h-Ghost. Itchy wheals appear and vanish within hours.
cards.lore: IgE-mediated mast cell explosion. Here now, gone by morning.
cards.gradeReason: 24h-Ghost is a great POWER name; full performance needs knowing the mast-cell trigger.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: transparent ghost covered in hive welts, fading in and out. Mood: ephemeral itch.

cards.power: The Great Peel. Skin sloughs off in large sheets like a severe burn.
cards.lore: Usually a violent drug reaction. Naïve to pools, hotels, anything.
cards.gradeReason: The Great Peel with TEN stat = harrowing, impossible to forget.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: tragic wrestler peeling layers away in huge sheets, hospital background. Mood: catastrophic.

cards.power: The Insulin Shadow. Dark, velvety hyperpigmentation in neck and axilla creases.
cards.lore: Sign of insulin resistance or hidden malignancy. Soft warning.
cards.gradeReason: Velvet Neck is tactile; Insulin Shadow is clever — but LORE explains rather than charges.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: velvet-collared character with dark neck creases, subtle insulin-syringe motif. Mood: diagnostic whisper.

cards.power: The White-Out. Autoimmune depigmentation spreads in irregular patches.
cards.lore: Autoimmune attack against Mel the shield-maker. Skin left totally unprotected.
cards.gradeReason: The Ghost is evocative; Mel-callback is lovely — but POWER is descriptive not action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: translucent ghost wrestler with stark white patches defeating a small melanocyte. Mood: haunting loss.

cards.power: The Gluten Sting. Extremely itchy papulovesicles on elbows and knees.
cards.lore: Harry always teams up with gluten intolerance. Legendary itch.
cards.gradeReason: Gluten Sting is fun; but 'Harry' for Dermatitis Herpetiformis needs context to decode.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: itchy wrestler in wheat-sheaf armor attacking elbows and knees. Mood: inflamed, relentless.

cards.power: The Dirty Sticker. Looks like a greasy, brown wart just stuck onto the skin. Harmless.
cards.lore: If Sid appears in massive numbers suddenly, suspect an internal tumor.
cards.gradeReason: Just stuck onto the skin — you feel Sid's texture through the words.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: greasy brown sticker-character pasted casually onto a skin surface. Mood: harmless but eerie in bulk.

cards.power: The Ruby Drop. Small, bright red, pinhead-sized dots that increase with age.
cards.lore: Harmless pooling of small blood vessels; purely esthetic, please.
cards.gradeReason: Ruby Drop is sweet; POWER is visual description, not an invitation to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: cheerful cherry-red dot character multiplying with age on skin surface. Mood: benign accumulation.

cards.power: The Incriminating Sheet. Forms bluish-purple patches and nodules in immunocompromised wrestlers.
cards.lore: A vascular tumor powered by Human Herpesvirus 8. Classic in AIDS.
cards.gradeReason: Incriminating Sheet is vivid; LORE is clear but explains more than it performs.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: purple-patched villain spreading across immunocompromised fighter's skin. Mood: opportunistic, sinister.

cards.power: The Fountain. Red, shiny nodule that bleeds like a fountain at the slightest touch.
cards.lore: NOT a true granuloma. An overgrowth of vessels following a minor injury.
cards.gradeReason: Bleeds like a fountain at the slightest touch — you wince before you're done reading.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: shiny red geyser-character erupting at the lightest tap. Mood: dramatic over-reaction.

cards.power: The Rogue Scar. Won't stop building after an injury, growing far beyond the original wound.
cards.lore: More common in darker skin types. Often itches and is heavily therapy-resistant.
cards.gradeReason: Won't stop building — Kelly's entire character is her refusal to stop.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: scar-tissue wrestler bursting beyond wound boundaries, still growing. Mood: relentless construction.

cards.power: The Scale Armor. Entire skin is dry and covered in large, adherent scales.
cards.lore: Kevin the brick fails to shed. Massive water loss through the defective barrier.
cards.gradeReason: Fish Man + Scale Armor + Kevin callback = three layers of brilliance at once.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: fish-scaled wrestler shedding cracked plates with Kevin-bricks visible underneath. Mood: ancient, layered.

cards.power: The Yellow Bump. Yellowish papules or plates, especially on eyelids.
cards.lore: Xavier is a messenger—he warns that there is too much cholesterol in the blood.
cards.gradeReason: Yellowish papules on eyelids — describes appearance, not a role to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: yellow-patched herald character waving cholesterol-warning flag near eye. Mood: urgent messenger.

cards.power: The Mother Patch. Starts with a large herald patch, then scatters small scale-islands.
cards.lore: Likely viral. Heals alone in 6-8 weeks. Follows the skin's tension lines.
cards.gradeReason: Mother Patch is evocative; self-resolution lore is reassuring but not performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: herald character unfurling a Christmas-tree pattern across the torso. Mood: temporary, self-resolving.

cards.power: The Inflammation Freeze. Puts out every fire instantly. All-purpose weapon for redness and itch.
cards.lore: Long-term use causes atrophy—thins the skin like parchment paper!
cards.gradeReason: Puts out every fire instantly — Stella's power and danger in one sweep.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: ice-shield wielder dousing flames, but cracking parchment beneath feet. Mood: powerful but fragile.

cards.power: The Fast-Forward. Forces cells to mature and shed faster, clearing clogged pores.
cards.lore: Kryptonite for acne. Warning: highly teratogenic (no pregnancy).
cards.gradeReason: Kryptonite for acne + teratogenic warning — Rick is complete in two sentences.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: fast-forward button wrestler accelerating skin cells, pregnancy-warning badge prominently displayed. Mood: urgent.

cards.power: Releases free oxygen to simply blow up acne bacteria.
cards.lore: Radical cleaner. Ben will permanently bleach your linens and towels.
cards.gradeReason: Permanently bleach your linens — useful, funny, and absolutely true.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: oxygen-explosion character with bleach-stained cape blowing up bacteria. Mood: collateral-damage hero.

cards.power: The Growth Stopper. Tells Psoriasis-Pete's turbo-reconstruction to slow down.
cards.lore: Inhibits excessive cell division without thinning the skin like Stella does.
cards.gradeReason: Cal needs knowing Pete and Stella to land — intertextual but not fully self-standing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: calm referee placing hand on Pete's shoulder, stopping turbo-buildup. Mood: moderating presence.

cards.power: The Mite Assassin. Paralyzes the nerves of Scabies-Scott until they give up.
cards.lore: Standard scabies treatment. MUST be applied head-to-toe without any gaps.
cards.gradeReason: Mite Assassin is strong; LORE is instructional protocol, not performative invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: exterminator character zapping tiny mites from full-body head-to-toe coverage. Mood: thorough extermination.

cards.power: The Wall Breaker. Prevents fungi from building their cell membranes.
cards.lore: Terry accumulates in nails and skin over time for sustained attack.
cards.gradeReason: Wall Breaker works well; sustained accumulation adds depth without full punch.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: demolition character smashing a fungal membrane wall with a sledgehammer. Mood: methodical destruction.

cards.power: Modern high-end cytokine weapon for severe eczema. Targeted cytokine communication block.
cards.lore: Shuts down the exact signals that destroy Atopic-Alice's wall.
cards.gradeReason: IL-Sniper is vivid; Alice-callback is great — but needs knowing the signaling cascade.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: sniper character targeting floating IL-4/IL-13 signals mid-air, protecting cracked wall behind. Mood: precision.

cards.power: The Fade Out. Stops Mel the shield-maker and lightens dark spots.
cards.lore: Bleaching cream. Interrupts pigment production directly in the basal lab.
cards.gradeReason: Stops Mel is a fun intertextual move; LORE is instructional but basal lab metaphor saves it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: bleach-bottle character fading Mel's pigment shields into white. Mood: controlled erasure.

cards.power: The Deep Look. Reveals pigment networks and vessel patterns invisible to the naked eye.
cards.lore: Distinguishes a harmless sticker (Sid) from a dangerous shadow (Mel).
cards.gradeReason: Sid vs. Mel reference is perfect — Dash knows everybody and their secrets.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: magnifying-lens detective character examining skin, Sid and Mel visible in lens. Mood: Sherlock authority.

cards.power: Makes fungi glow green and certain bacteria glow coral-red under UV light.
cards.lore: Used for tinea versicolor, erythrasma, and porphyria diagnosis.
cards.gradeReason: The glow colors are genuinely memorable; LORE is list-like rather than inviting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: UV-torch wielder illuminating green-glowing fungi and red bacteria. Mood: blacklight revelation.

cards.power: Tapes suspects to the back to see if an alarm triggers days later.
cards.lore: Finds the cause of Type IV contact allergies. Do NOT confuse with immediate prick tests!
cards.gradeReason: Tapes suspects to the back — clinical procedure as wrestling detainment move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: detective character taping small allergen-squares to wrestler's back in grid. Mood: methodical investigation.

cards.power: The Final Word. Takes a tiny piece of the wrestler to the lab to clarify true identity.
cards.lore: When Dash and Wanda are unsure, Bill provides the definitive microscopic look.
cards.gradeReason: The Punch biopsy as wrestling move — clinical precision as a finishing move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: punch-biopsy tool character delivering a decisive jab into skin, lab flask in other hand. Mood: conclusive.

cards.power: The Patchy Loss. Hair falls out in smooth, circular patches.
cards.lore: T cells attack the follicle junction, triggering sudden, shock-round hair loss.
cards.gradeReason: Patchy Loss describes outcome; the card tells you what happens, not what to do.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: fighter with smooth circular bald patches mid-match, T-cell attackers visible. Mood: sudden loss.

cards.power: Minnie opens vessels; Fin stops the toxin shrinking the roots.
cards.lore: Standard combo for male-pattern hair loss. Requires months of patience.
cards.gradeReason: Dual character concept is clever; months of patience is practical, not performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: tag-team pair — Minnie with vasodilator pump, Fin with DHT-blocker shield. Mood: slow comeback.

cards.power: Makes nails yellow, thick, and brittle. Deeply stubborn tenant.
cards.lore: Creams cannot penetrate the hard nail-shield; requires systemic oral therapy.
cards.gradeReason: Deeply stubborn tenant is a great metaphor; POWER is more describe-then-act.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: stubborn fungus squatter embedded in a yellow nail fortress. Mood: eviction-proof.

cards.power: The Pus Demand. Throbs intensely until the pus is released.
cards.lore: Caused by minor injuries. If it throbs intensely, the pus demands to get out!
cards.gradeReason: The pus demands to get out — Pat is the most relatable villain in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: swollen nail-fold character pounding fist, pus-bubble pressurizing from inside. Mood: urgent, throbbing.

cards.power: The Pimp-Master. Forces every player to name, classify, and justify every lesion.
cards.lore: Describe the primary lesion! Is it a macule, a papule, or a plaque? Identity the border or leave the clinic.
cards.gradeReason: The Attending as enforcer-card is pedagogical theater — you ARE on rounds.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wrestling card. Subject: stern attending physician-referee demanding lesion descriptions from all players. Mood: high-pressure education.

cards.lore: 30-year-old wrestler has silvery scales on elbows. Scraping a scale leads to pinpoint bleeding.
cards.gradeReason: Clinical vignette as a challenge duel — Auspitz phenomenon becomes a finishing move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: quest card. Subject: silver-scaled elbow under a magnifying lens with pinpoint blood drops. Mood: diagnostic tension.

cards.lore: Student itching to death at night. Small burrows between fingers.
cards.gradeReason: Itching to death at night + burrows = Scabies-Scott identified before you finish reading.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: quest card. Subject: nocturnal student scratching between fingers with mite-tunnel visible under blacklight. Mood: frantic clue-hunt.

cards.lore: After new meds, patient gets fever and skin peels off in massive sheets.
cards.gradeReason: Skin peels off in massive sheets after new meds — SJS-Terry unmistakable and horrifying.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: quest card. Subject: patient's skin mask falling away post-medication, hospital setting. Mood: urgent catastrophe.

verdict: The Great Barrier Brawl is MedKayfab at its most architecturally sound — the opening four-card wall crew (Kevin, Desmo, Mel, Lance) sets the arena before a single disease character enters, a design move that pays dividends across all 56 cards. Quest cards on the final page turn clinical vignettes into naming duels, an innovation that should ship to every other MedKayfab deck. Named weakness: dual Rose characters (Rosacea-Rose, Pityriasis-Rose) will collide at table without a naming fix. Table-ready: Yes.
blurb: For med students who want to stop memorizing and start performing. 56 skin-wrestling characters from Keratin-Kevin to Biopsy-Bill, plus 3 clinical vignette Quest cards. Derm finally makes sense.

coverQA.coverVisual: 4 — Dense wrestling-arena composition with multiple skin characters visible; energetic if complex.
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — The Great Barrier Brawl is exactly right: clinical, punchy, self-explaining.
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Cover vibes match deck contents precisely; barrier metaphor carried throughout.
coverQA.coverOriginality: 4 — Distinctive within MedKayfab branding; consistent with series visual language.
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — Shareable among med students and derm residents; wrestling + dermatology combo is clickbait.
coverQA.coverNote: The Great Barrier Brawl title does the heavy lifting. Cover art delivers on the wrestling-derm promise without overexplaining. Strong entry point for the MedKayfab brand.

notes: All 15 pages are fully image-based (raster PDF); OCR was required throughout. Decorative fonts on STAT fields and card numbers created ~8 font artifact cases. Notable structural innovation: last page features 3 clinical Quest vignette cards + The Attending enforcer card, turning the final page into a clinical exam round. Dual 'Rose' naming: Rosacea-Rose (card 22) and Pityriasis-Rose (card 36) will confuse at table — one should be renamed. Treatment cluster (cards 37-44) is cohesive as a 'medication' roster but some cards lean instructional in LORE.

urgent: Rename either Rosacea-Rose or Pityriasis-Rose — dual Rose naming will collide at table
quickWins: Quest cards need explicit QUEST: answer field (currently only in LORE)
niceToHave: Treatment cluster (37-44) could get a visual 'RX' badge to distinguish from disease cards
Erythema-Nodosum-Nora POWER text could be strengthened — currently underplays septal panniculitis drama

marketingText:
MedKayfab: DERMATOLOGY – The Great Barrier Brawl (Medical Mnemonics Cut & Play Comic)

56 illustrated medical mnemonic cards to master the skin barrier and the ways it breaks, the acne and eczema you will treat in every single clinic, and the pigmented lesion whose depth decides who walks out alive.

Everyone tells you dermatology is the soft option. Clinic hours, no nights, a wall of rashes that all look the same and none of them page you at 3am. Then on your first rotation an attending drops a lesion the size of a pencil eraser in front of you and asks how deep it goes, because the answer in millimetres is the line between a five-minute excision and a funeral. The skin is the one organ the whole world gets to touch, the wall you never think about until the day it fails and you have to read it out loud.

MedKayfab Dermatology turns the barrier and everything that lays siege to it into a narrative wrestling match. Stop memorizing rash descriptions as flat vocabulary. Start performing each disease as a fighter with a method, a tell, and a counter.

YOU'LL GET
- 56 illustrated MedKayfab cards (14pp, 4 cards/page)
- Full MedKayfab Freestyle rules (Quest Die mechanics), including a closing clinical exam round where three Quest vignettes and The Attending grill you the way a real ward round does
- S-Tier characters like Keratin-Kevin (The Brick), Biopsy-Bill (The Punch), and Melanoma-Mel (The Dark Shadow)
- Free lifetime updates as guidelines evolve
- CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence, print, share, and adapt freely
- PDF optimized for home printing (A4 / Letter)

What's in the deck
The whole specialty is built on a wall, and this deck makes you meet the bricks. Keratin-Kevin, The Brick, is the dead-cell barrier that holds your water in and the world out, and most of the diseases in here are the story of that wall failing at one specific seam. Biopsy-Bill, The Punch, is the small circular cut you reach for when the naked eye runs out of answers and the tissue has to testify under glass. Melanoma-Mel, The Dark Shadow, is the one fighter who measures his own depth, because here the prognosis is written in millimetres and nobody gets to argue with the ruler. Benzoyl-Ben, the Oxygen Bomb, anchors a full treatment roster, so the deck never stops at naming the enemy, it hands you the counters.

How it works
Every card is a cognitive anchor. You have the Character (the mnemonic), the Visual (the scene), the Stat Block (the numbers that matter), the Lore (the clinical story), and the Quest (the challenge). The Mechanism Flash mode is the brutal part: explain the lesion or the drug in one sentence without looking, or the patient on the Stage walks out undiagnosed. The deck then escalates into its exam round, where The Midnight Tunnel and two more Quest vignettes put everything you just learned in front of The Attending, who does not grade on kindness.

Honest cognitive load
This is a clinical-years and rotation deck. It rewards a student who has already met basic histology and immunology, because half the fights in here are barrier and hypersensitivity mechanisms wearing a rash. It pairs cleanly with Immunology & Pathology for the autoimmune and blistering diseases, and with Internal Medicine for the times the skin is simply the first place a systemic illness chose to announce itself. Heavy on pattern recognition, light on math.

ABOUT MEDKAYFAB
MedKayfab is a narrative medical learning card game, 50 decks covering the full medical curriculum. Every card encodes a clinical mechanism as a character with a personality, a story, and a reasoning challenge. Built by a physician. Assembled with AI tools. Manually revised. Honest about its limitations. Free to use, share, and adapt under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

PAY WHAT YOU WANT
This deck is Pay What You Want, including free. If you find it useful, a fair price is €5. If you are a student on a budget, enter €0, no questions asked. If you want to support more decks, anything above fair price is appreciated. Share freely, attribute honestly, never resell.

DISCLAIMER
MedKayfab is a learning companion, not a clinical reference. Content was created by a physician and reviewed to the best of our knowledge, but medicine evolves, guidelines change, and some mechanisms in here will be simplified or wrong. Always verify against current primary sources and clinical guidelines before applying anything to patient care. The Blödsinn! is the vehicle. The science is serious.

Stay fluffy. — Doc FrizzleBob
